scenes.title: A pitch default with local exceptions

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device on OUT 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major at 90 BPM, with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). All Trig params slots are empty, and the Device page is showing.

steps.title: Find Fixed Note
steps.caption: Fixed Note makes the channel send one chosen MIDI note while the pattern still decides when. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Trig params with E2 and press K3. Press K2 to open the parameter list and turn E3 until it shows Fixed Note.

steps.title: Assign Fixed Note to a slot
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Fixed Note to the first slot and K2 to return. Slot 1 reads X, which means Off, so the parameter is assigned but sends nothing yet.

steps.title: Set the channel pitch
steps.caption: With no step held, turn E3 to 60 (C3). Slot 1 reads C5, this slot's name for MIDI note 60 (it numbers octaves two higher than the C3 used elsewhere in this manual). This is the channel's default pitch, the note every step plays unless it has its own lock.

steps.title: Play the default
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The MIDI strip lists four C3 (60) note-ons at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The pitch is fixed and the velocities are not.

steps.title: Give step 2 another pitch
steps.caption: Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 to 63 (D#3) and release. A value set on a held step is a lock, and it belongs to step 2 alone. Play, then stop: the strip reads 60, 63, 60, 60 (C3, D#3, C3, C3).

steps.title: Zero is a note
steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 down to 0 and release. 0 is a real pitch, the lowest MIDI note (C-2), not Off. Play, then stop: the strip reads 0, 63, 60, 60.

steps.title: X is no lock; raise the default beneath the locks
steps.caption: Hold step 4 at (4,4), turn E3 down to X (Off) and release. X on a step means no lock, and step 4 had none, so a Play and Stop still gives 0, 63, 60, 60. Then, with no step held, turn E3 up five detents to raise the channel pitch to 65 (F3), and Play and Stop again: steps 3 and 4 follow the new default and steps 1 and 2 keep their locks, 0, 63, 65, 65.

steps.title: Clear a lock, then turn the channel pitch off
steps.caption: Hold step 2, press K2 and release: its lock is gone, so Play and Stop gives 0, 65, 65, 65. Then, with no step held, turn E3 down to X (Off), and Play and Stop again: steps 2, 3 and 4 return to the written phrase, 62, 64, 65, while step 1 still plays its own lock, 0.

steps.title: Clear the last lock
steps.caption: Hold step 1, press K2 and release. With no lock and no channel pitch left, Play and Stop gives the original C, D, E, F phrase again: 60, 62, 64, 65.

scenes.title: Lock a value, then clear just that step

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device on OUT 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major at 90 BPM, with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Trig params screen is open on its parameter list, showing Fixed Note; every slot is empty (None).

steps.title: Set the channel default
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Fixed Note to the first slot and K2 to return. With no step held, turn E3 to 60 (C3). Play, then stop: the MIDI strip lists C3 (60) on all four steps.

steps.title: Lock one step
steps.caption: Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 to 63 (D#3) and release. A value set on a held step is a lock. Play, then stop: step 2 plays 63 and the other steps keep the default, 60, 63, 60, 60.

steps.title: Lock a second step
steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 down to 0 and release. Play, then stop: 0, 63, 60, 60. Zero is a real note, not Off.

steps.title: Raise the default beneath the locks
steps.caption: Hold step 4, turn E3 down to X (Off) and release: a step at X has no lock, so it follows the default. Then, with no step held, turn E3 up five detents to 65. Play, then stop: 0, 63, 65, 65. Steps 1 and 2 keep their locks.

steps.title: Let the default apply again
steps.caption: Hold step 2 at (2,4), press K2 and release: its lock is cleared and step 2 returns to the default. Play, then stop: 0, 65, 65, 65. Step 1 keeps its MIDI 0 lock; steps 2 to 4 follow the default. To lock a CC value the same way, see Brighten the last note with a cutoff lock.

scenes.title: Keep a default beneath your step edits

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device on OUT 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major at 90 BPM, with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Trig params screen is open on its parameter list, showing Fixed Note; every slot is empty (None).

steps.title: Choose a default
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Fixed Note to the selected slot and K2 to return. With no step held, turn E3 to 60: the slot's default is MIDI 60 (C3), used on every step that has no lock of its own. Tap Play (1,8), then Stop: the MIDI strip lists 60, 60, 60, 60.

steps.title: Lock a step
steps.caption: Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 to 63 and release. That is a lock: it applies to step 2 only. Play, then stop: 60, 63, 60, 60.

steps.title: Lock step 1 to zero
steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 down to 0 and release. 0 is a note, not Off. Play, then stop: 0, 63, 60, 60.

steps.title: Move the default
steps.caption: Hold step 4 at (4,4), turn E3 all the way down to X (Off) and release: a step at X has no lock and keeps following the default (0, 63, 60, 60 on Play and Stop). Then, with no step held, turn E3 up five detents to raise the default to 65. Play, then stop: 0, 63, 65, 65. Steps 1 and 2 keep their locks; steps 3 and 4 follow the new default.

scenes.title: Quantised pitch: the default and its exceptions

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device on OUT 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major at 90 BPM, with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Trig params screen is open on its parameter list, showing Quantised Fixed Note; no slot is assigned yet. Quantised Fixed Note works like Fixed Note, but snaps every value to the nearest note of the active scale, here C major.

steps.title: Assign Quantised Fixed Note to a slot
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Quantised Fixed Note to the first slot and K2 to return. Slot 1 reads X, which means Off.

steps.title: Set the channel pitch
steps.caption: With no step held, turn E3 to 60 (C3). Slot 1 reads 60, the channel's default pitch.

steps.title: Play the default
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The MIDI strip lists C3 (60) four times at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, exactly as in the Fixed Note example, because 60 is in the key.

steps.title: Lock step 2 to a pitch outside the key
steps.caption: Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 to 63 (D#3) and release. 63 is not in C major, so the lock snaps to the nearest scale note; D3 (62) and E3 (64) are equally close and the lower one wins. Play, then stop: the strip reads 60, 62, 60, 60. The Fixed Note example plays 63 here.

steps.title: Zero is a note
steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 down to 0 and release. 0 is a real pitch, not Off, and it is in the key. Play, then stop: the strip reads 0, 62, 60, 60.

steps.title: Raise the default beneath the locks
steps.caption: Hold step 4 at (4,4), turn E3 down to X (Off) and release: step 4 had no lock, so nothing changes (0, 62, 60, 60 on Play and Stop). Then, with no step held, turn E3 up five detents to raise the channel pitch to 65 (F3, in the key). Play, then stop: steps 3 and 4 follow it and steps 1 and 2 keep their locks, 0, 62, 65, 65. Clearing locks and turning the channel pitch off behave exactly as in the Fixed Note example, A pitch default with local exceptions.

scenes.title: Turn chance into explicit rests

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. Every trig has its normal chance of sounding. The Trig params screen is open on its parameter list, showing Fixed Note; no slot is assigned yet. Fixed Note is used here to pin the pitch, so that you hear only which trigs play, not which note.

steps.title: Fix the pitch, then find Trig Probability
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Fixed Note to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 to 65 (F3): every note is now F3. Turn E2 to the next slot and open the Trig Probability picker.

steps.title: Assign the probability slot
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Trig Probability and K2 to return. The selected slot reads X until you set its channel value.

steps.title: Confirm the channel probability
steps.caption: Set the selected Trig Probability slot to 100 and check its readout before auditioning the phrase.

steps.title: 100 plays every trig, and nothing goes above it
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Trig Probability and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 100. Tap Play (1,8) and tap it again to stop: the MIDI strip lists all four steps at pitch 65 with velocities 127, 117, 107, 97. Then turn E3 up a few more detents; the value stays at 100. Play and stop again: every trig still sounds.

steps.title: Confirm zero chance on the channel
steps.caption: With no step held, set Trig Probability to 0 and confirm the slot readout has no L lock marker.

steps.title: Start the zero-probability audition
steps.caption: Tap Play and confirm the transport indicator turns on before the bounded audition window.

steps.title: Stop the zero-probability audition
steps.caption: Tap Play/Stop again and confirm the transport indicator turns off.

steps.title: 0 is a certain rest
steps.caption: At 0, none of the four trigs plays a note. Compare this with 100, where every trig plays.

steps.title: Confirm the step-two override
steps.caption: While step 2 is held, the Trig Probability slot reads 100 with an L marker.

steps.title: Confirm the channel value after release
steps.caption: After step 2 is released, the channel probability remains 0.

steps.title: Let one step through
steps.caption: Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 all the way down and then up to 100, and release. That lock beats the channel's 0. Tap Play: only step 2 sounds, once per loop, at velocity 117. The channel value is still 0.

steps.title: Confirm the channel value before the local edit
steps.caption: The channel Trig Probability is 100 before step 1 receives its own lock.

steps.title: Confirm the first-step rest lock
steps.caption: While step 1 is held, the Trig Probability slot reads 0 with an L marker.

steps.title: Confirm the channel value after release
steps.caption: After step 1 is released, the channel probability remains 100.

steps.title: Reject one step
steps.caption: With no step held, turn E3 up to 100 again. Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 all the way down and one detent up to 0, and release. A lock of 0 beats the channel's 100. Tap Play: step 1 is silent and steps 2, 3 and 4 sound.

steps.title: Confirm the wrap-step rest lock
steps.caption: While step 4 is held, the Trig Probability slot reads 0 with an L marker.

steps.title: Confirm the channel value after release
steps.caption: After step 4 is released, the channel probability remains 100.

steps.title: Reject a second step
steps.caption: Hold step 4 at (4,4), set its lock to 0 the same way and release. Tap Play: steps 2 and 3 sound; steps 1 and 4 are silent.

steps.title: Clear both locks
steps.caption: Hold step 1, press K2 and release. Tap Play: steps 1, 2 and 3 sound, and step 4 is still silent. Then hold step 4, press K2 and release. Tap Play: all four steps sound again.

scenes.title: Explore a bounded random contour

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. In PARAMS > MOSAIC, Lock random to pent. and Lock merged to pent. are Off, so offsets can land on any note of the scale. Random Note is already assigned to the first Trig params slot, and the parameter list is open for the second slot, on Twos Random Note (the manual's Random Twos Note).

steps.title: Offset 0 leaves the phrase alone
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Twos Random Note to the second slot and K2 to return, then press E2 to select the first slot, Random Note. Both slots read 0. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop: the phrase is unchanged, 60, 62, 64, 65.

steps.title: Turn Random Note up to 1, then 2
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent to Random Note 1: each note is its original degree or the next one up the scale. Play and stop (first pass 60, 64, 64, 65). Then turn E3 to 2: each note is its degree, one above or one below. Play and stop (first pass 59, 60, 62, 67). The MIDI strip shows this manual's fixed random run, which repeats exactly; on your norns the notes change on every pass, but always stay within the offsets named here.

steps.title: Turn Random Note up to 3, then 4
steps.caption: Turn E3 to 3: each note may move -1, 0, +1 or +2. Play and stop (first pass 60, 60, 67, 69). Then turn E3 to 4: each note may move -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees. Play and stop (first pass 57, 64, 67, 62).

steps.title: Add Twos Random Note on top
steps.caption: Turn E2 to the Twos Random Note slot, turn E3 to 4, then turn E2 back and play. The two offsets add, so each note may move anywhere from -6 to +6 scale degrees. First pass: 57, 59, 55, 64.

scenes.title: Explore a bounded random contour in thirds

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. In PARAMS > MOSAIC, Lock random to pent. and Lock merged to pent. are Off, so offsets can land on any note of the scale. Random Note is already assigned to the first Trig params slot, and the parameter list is open for the second slot, on Twos Random Note (the manual's Random Twos Note), which is the slot you will turn.

steps.title: Offset 0 leaves the phrase alone
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Twos Random Note to the second slot and K2 to return, then press E2 to select the first slot, Random Note. Both slots read 0. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop: the phrase is unchanged, 60, 62, 64, 65.

steps.title: Turn Twos Random Note up to 1, then 2
steps.caption: Turn E2 to the second slot, Twos Random Note, turn E3 one detent to 1 and turn E2 back: each note is its original degree or two degrees higher. Play and stop (first pass 60, 65, 64, 65). Then repeat to set 2: each note may move -2, 0 or +2 degrees. Play and stop (first pass 57, 59, 60, 69). The MIDI strip shows this manual's fixed random run, which repeats exactly; on your norns the notes change on every pass, but always stay within the offsets named here.

steps.title: Turn Twos Random Note up to 3, then 4
steps.caption: Repeat the E2, E3, E2 turn to set 3: each note may move -2, 0, +2 or +4 degrees. Play and stop (first pass 60, 59, 71, 72). Then set 4: each note may move -4, -2, 0, +2 or +4 degrees, leaps of thirds wider than Random Note's single steps. Play and stop (first pass 53, 65, 71, 59).

steps.title: Add Random Note on top
steps.caption: With the first slot, Random Note, selected, turn E3 to 4, then play. The two offsets add: each note may move anywhere from -6 to +6 scale degrees. First pass: 57, 59, 55, 64.

scenes.title: Choose a supported musical division

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. You are on the Trig params screen with the parameter list open on Chord Note Strum; no Trig params slot is assigned yet. Divisions are counted in channel steps, from 1/24 of a step up to 128 steps, and X means Off.

steps.title: Assign it: a new slot starts at X
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Strum to the first slot, then K2 to return to the slot list. The slot reads X, which means Off: no strum, so a chord's notes still sound together.

steps.title: X is the lowest setting
steps.caption: With no step held, turn E3 down three detents. The slot stays at X; there is nothing below Off.

steps.title: One detent up: the shortest division
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent up from X. The slot reads 1/24, the shortest division: one twenty-fourth of a channel step.

steps.title: Top of the range, then one step back
steps.caption: Hold E3 turning right, about ninety detents, until the slot reads 128 channel steps; further turns leave it at 128. Then turn one detent back: the slot reads 120, the next supported value below the limit. For a musical setting, see Separate a chord into timed voices, which uses a half-step strum.

scenes.title: Assign one slot and read its value

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device on OUT 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major at 90 BPM, with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Device page is showing, and the ten Trig params slots are all empty (None). Any parameter is assigned the same way; Chord Note Strum is used here only because its values are quick to turn through.

steps.title: Open the parameter list
steps.caption: Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Trig params with E2 and press K3. Press K2 to open the parameter list and turn E3 to Chord Note Strum.

steps.title: An assigned slot starts at X
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Strum to the first slot and K2 to return. The slot shows its short name (Chrd Strm) and the value X. X means Off: the parameter sends nothing. The next scenes use Fixed Note and CC 1 the same way.

steps.title: Edit the selected slot
steps.caption: With no step held, turn E3 down three detents (the slot stays at X), then one detent up. The slot reads 1/24, the shortest strum division. Turn E3 further for other divisions; turning back to X switches the strum off.

You are on the Trig params screen with the parameter list open on Chord Note Arpeggio; no Trig params slot is assigned yet. scenes.title: Choose a Spread duration

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. You are on the Trig params screen with the parameter list open on Chord Spread; no Trig params slot is assigned yet. Spread only widens the gaps of a Strum or Arpeggio that is switched on, so nothing is switched on here and you will hear no change. Divisions are counted in channel steps, from 1/24 of a step up to 128 steps, and X means Off.

steps.title: Assign it: a new slot starts at X
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread to the first slot, then K2 to return to the slot list. The slot reads X, which means Off: no extra gap is added.

steps.title: X is the lowest setting
steps.caption: With no step held, turn E3 down three detents. The slot stays at X; there is nothing below Off.

steps.title: One detent up: the shortest division
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent up from X. The slot reads 1/24, the shortest division: one twenty-fourth of a channel step.

steps.title: Top of the range, then one step back
steps.caption: Hold E3 turning right, about ninety detents, until the slot reads 128 channel steps; further turns leave it at 128. Then turn one detent back: the slot reads 120, the next supported value below the limit. For a musical setting, see Add a constant gap to the strum.

scenes.title: Separate a chord into timed voices

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Note Strum. No slot is assigned yet, so the five notes would sound together.

steps.title: Verify the half-step Strum value
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Strum to slot 1 and K2 to return. Turn E3 to 1/2. Slot 1 now shows 1/2 with no L or S marker; pause here before moving to another slot.

steps.title: Choose the chord pattern slot
steps.caption: From the verified half-step Strum slot, turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Pattern.

steps.title: Hear the strummed chord
steps.caption: Finish the setup the next examples reuse: assign Chord Pattern and turn E3 one detent to -> (forward); Assign Mute Chord Root and leave it at X so the root still sounds; then assign Chord Velocity Mod and turn E3 to +10 (E2 moves to the next slot, K2 opens the list, E3 browses, K3 assigns, K2 returns). Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip the notes arrive one after another, half a step apart: C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72). With Strum at X they would all start together.

scenes.title: Order the five chord slots

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Pattern. Chord Note Strum is already assigned and set to 1/2, half a step.

steps.title: Choose forward order
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Pattern and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent to -> (forward). Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Mute Chord Root.

steps.title: Hear the root first
steps.caption: Assign Mute Chord Root and leave it at X so the root still sounds; then assign Chord Velocity Mod and turn E3 to +10 (E2 moves to the next slot, K2 opens the list, E3 browses, K3 assigns, K2 returns). Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The five slots are the root and Chd1 to Chd4. The MIDI strip lists them in that order, half a step apart, root first: C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72).

scenes.title: Raise velocity up the chord

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Velocity Mod. Chord Note Strum (1/2), Chord Pattern (-> forward) and Mute Chord Root (X, off) are already assigned, so the root and four chord notes strum half a step apart.

steps.title: Raise each voice by 10
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Velocity Mod and K2 to return, then turn E3 up ten detents to +10. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip the notes C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72) carry velocities 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90: each note is 10 louder than the one before, so the chord swells upward.

scenes.title: Give every arp voice its own gate

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Note Arpeggio. No slot is assigned yet.

steps.title: Set a half-step Arpeggio
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Arpeggio to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/2. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Pattern.

steps.title: Hear a gate on every voice
steps.caption: An arpeggio gives every note its own gate: each note lasts one division, here half a step, from its own start. A strummed note is held to the end of the step. Assign Chord Pattern and turn E3 one detent to -> (forward); Assign Mute Chord Root and leave it at X so the root still sounds; then assign Chord Velocity Mod and turn E3 to +10 (E2 moves to the next slot, K2 opens the list, E3 browses, K3 assigns, K2 returns). Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip the five voices start half a step apart: C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72).

scenes.title: Reverse the slot order

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Pattern. Chord Note Strum is already assigned and set to 1/2, half a step.

steps.title: Choose reverse order
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Pattern and K2 to return, then turn E3 two detents to <- (reverse). Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Mute Chord Root.

steps.title: Hear the root last
steps.caption: Assign Mute Chord Root and leave it at X so the root still sounds; then assign Chord Velocity Mod and turn E3 to +10 (E2 moves to the next slot, K2 opens the list, E3 browses, K3 assigns, K2 returns). Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The order flips: C4 (72), A3 (69), G3 (67), E3 (64), then the root C3 (60), still half a step apart. The three Chord Pattern values are X (no shape), -> (forward) and <- (reverse).

scenes.title: Remove the root without collapsing time

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Mute Chord Root. Chord Note Strum (1/2) and Chord Pattern (-> forward) are already assigned; Mute Chord Root is not.

steps.title: Switch Mute Chord Root On
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Mute Chord Root and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent to On. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Velocity Mod.

steps.title: Play without the root
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Velocity Mod and K2 to return, then turn E3 to +10. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The MIDI strip lists four notes, not five: the root C3 (60) is silent, but the chord notes keep their places, E3 (64) half a step in at velocity 60, G3 (67) at one step (70), A3 (69) at 1 1/2 steps (80) and C4 (72) at two steps (90). With Mute Chord Root at X, 60 would sound first at velocity 50.

scenes.title: Stop when the next gap closes

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Only Chd1 (E, 64) and Chd4 (C, 72) are set, so Chd2 and Chd3 are empty slots; the output is polyphonic. Chord Note Strum is 1/2, Chord Pattern is <- (reverse: slot 4, 3, 2, 1, then the root), Mute Chord Root is assigned and left at X, and Chord Velocity Mod is +10. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Spread; Spread and Chord Accel Mod are not assigned yet.

steps.title: Set a quarter-step Spread
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/4. Each gap is now 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4 step. Acceleration works on Spread, so with Spread at zero it would do nothing. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Accel Mod.

steps.title: A faster reverse strum can end early
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Accel Mod and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent down to -1: each gap is a quarter step (Spread x 1) shorter than the one before. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The gaps are 3/4, 1/2 and 1/4 step, and the gap after that would be 0, so scheduling stops. Slot 4 (C4, 72) sounds at once, empty slots 3 and 2 pass in silence at 3/4 and 1 1/4 steps, and slot 1 (E3, 64) sounds 1 1/2 steps after the trigger. The MIDI strip lists only those two notes; the root C3 (60) never sounds.

scenes.title: Slow the strum down with Accel +1

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Only Chd1 (E, 64) and Chd4 (C, 72) are set, so Chd2 and Chd3 are empty slots; the output is polyphonic. Chord Note Strum is 1/2, Chord Pattern is <- (reverse: slot 4, 3, 2, 1, then the root), Mute Chord Root is assigned and left at X, and Chord Velocity Mod is +10. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Spread; Spread and Chord Accel Mod are not assigned yet.

steps.title: Set a quarter-step Spread
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/4. Each gap is now 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4 step. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Accel Mod.

steps.title: A positive Accel makes each gap longer
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Accel Mod and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent up to +1: each gap is a quarter step (Spread x 1) longer than the one before. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The gaps are 3/4, 1, 1 1/4 and 1 1/2 steps, so slot 4 (C4, 72) sounds at once, empty slots 3 and 2 pass in silence at 3/4 and 1 3/4 steps, slot 1 (E3, 64) sounds at 3 steps and the root C3 (60) at 4 1/2 steps. Look at the MIDI strip "MIDI sent in this step": the three notes arrive further and further apart.

scenes.title: Slow the strum with Spread

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, with Chd1 to Chd4 set to 64, 67, 69 and 72; the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Note Strum. Nothing is assigned yet.

steps.title: Set a half-step Strum
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Strum to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/2: the notes will be half a step apart. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Spread.

steps.title: Widen each gap for a slow, harp-like roll
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/4. Chord Accel Mod is not assigned, so every gap stays the same. Each gap is now 3/4 step (1/2 + 1/4) instead of 1/2. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The MIDI strip lists the root C3 (60) and then E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69), C4 (72), evenly spaced 3/4 step apart.

assertion.compatibility_claim: New-contract conformance; historical behavior is preserved only where independently shown

scenes.title: Move between parameter locks

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a device with MIDI CCs, at 90 BPM with Rate /1, so one step lasts a sixth of a second. PARAMS is open on the device's CC 1 control at its stored value, 63, set in PARAMS > MOSAIC. CC 1 is not assigned to a Trig params slot yet, and parameter slides are off.

steps.title: Find CC 1
steps.caption: Press K1 to leave PARAMS. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Trig params with E2 and press K3, then press K2 and turn E3 to CC 1 in the parameter list.

steps.title: Assign CC 1 to the slot
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign CC 1 and K2 to return. Slot 1 now reads 63, the stored value, with no marker in its corner, because no step has a lock for it yet.

steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24
steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4) and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held, so this step now has its own value for CC 1. Release the step.

steps.title: Lock step 3 to 96
steps.caption: Hold step 3 at (3,4) and turn E3 to 96. Slot 1 shows 96 with the L. Release the step. Steps 1 and 3 now carry different CC 1 values, two steps apart.

steps.title: Turn slides on for the parameter
steps.caption: With no step held, press K3. Slot 1 reads 63 again and gains an S in its corner, so every lock of CC 1 slides toward the next one.

steps.title: Play and watch the glide
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops play, then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip, CC 1 starts at 24 on step 1 and climbs in equal steps of 12, about every 56 ms: 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, reaching 96 as step 3's note starts. The glide fills the two steps between the locks.

steps.title: The device setting does not change
steps.caption: Press K1 to open PARAMS. CC 1 still shows its stored value, 63: playback never changes the setting you stored, so the glide exists only in the CC messages that were sent.

scenes.title: Slide only one source lock

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a device with MIDI CCs, at 90 BPM with Rate /1, so one step lasts a sixth of a second. PARAMS is open on the device's CC 1 control at its stored value, 63, set in PARAMS > MOSAIC. CC 1 is not assigned to a Trig params slot yet, and parameter slides are off. The previous scene turned slides on for the whole parameter; this one turns them on for a single step.

steps.title: Find CC 1
steps.caption: Press K1 to leave PARAMS. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Trig params with E2 and press K3, then press K2 and turn E3 to CC 1 in the parameter list.

steps.title: Assign CC 1 to the slot
steps.caption: Press K3 to assign CC 1 and K2 to return. Slot 1 now reads 63, the stored value, with no marker in its corner, because no step has a lock for it yet.

steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24
steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4) and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held. Release the step.

steps.title: Lock step 3 to 96
steps.caption: Hold step 3 at (3,4) and turn E3 to 96. Slot 1 shows 96 with the L. Release the step.

steps.title: Lock step 4 to 48
steps.caption: Hold step 4 at (4,4) and turn E3 to 48. Slot 1 shows 48 with the L. Release the step.

steps.title: Slide from step 1 only
steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4) and press K3. Slot 1 shows 24 with an S in its corner while step 1 is held, so only the slide that starts at step 1 is on. Release the step.

steps.title: Play and watch the glide stop at step 3
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops play, then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip, CC 1 glides from 24 to 96 in equal steps of 12 (36, 48, 60, 72, 84) between steps 1 and 3, then jumps straight to 48 at step 4 with no glide.

steps.title: The device setting does not change
steps.caption: Press K1 to open PARAMS. CC 1 still shows 63, the value you stored: the slide only shapes the messages sent while playing.

scenes.title: Choose what the final lock slides toward

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1-4 with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, at the default 90 BPM with Rate /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each); the sequencer is stopped. CC 1 is assigned to a Trig params slot and locked on three steps: 24 on step 1, 96 on step 3 and 48 on step 4; step 2 has no lock. Step 1's slide is off, and step 4's slide is on. Wrap param slides is Off, so there is no later lock for step 4 to slide toward: CC 1 holds at 48 until the loop restarts and the first lock, 24, is recalled with a jump.

steps.title: Turn on Wrap param slides
steps.caption: Press K1 to open PARAMS, go to the MOSAIC group, select Wrap param slides and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

steps.title: Slide back to the first lock
steps.caption: Press K1 to leave PARAMS, tap Play (1,8), let two loops play and tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip, CC 1 now descends from 48 to 24 across the loop boundary, 40, 32, 24 about 56 ms apart, and arrives at 24 together with the first note. A filter or other target sweeps smoothly around the loop.

scenes.title: Choose which note masks follow the scale

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1; both are already set in the scale editor. In PARAMS > MOSAIC, Snap note masks to scale is On, while Quantise note masks (the global full-quantisation option) and Lock merged to pent. are Off. With Snap alone the masks play as written, 60, 64, 69, 71 in the MIDI strip, because Degree and Rotation affect masks only under full quantisation. Quantise Note Mask works on three levels, strongest first: a step lock, then the channel value, then the global option. On follows the scale, Off keeps the written pitch, and X means inherit from the next level down. Each step below lists the state as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: Off / X / X / X.

steps.title: Global: turn full quantisation On
steps.caption: State: On / X / X / X. Press K1, open the Mosaic params and turn Quantise note masks On (the global option). Play, then stop: the same masks now follow Degree II and Rotation 1 and the strip reads 62, 65, 71, 60.

steps.title: Channel: an Off beats the global On
steps.caption: State: On / Off / X / X. Open Channel tasks > Trig params, press K2 and turn E3 to Quantise Note Mask in the parameter list. Press K3 to assign it and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent to Off. Play, then stop: the written phrase 60, 64, 69, 71 returns, because the channel setting beats the global On.

steps.title: Step: map just one step
steps.caption: State: On / Off / X / On. Hold step 2 and turn E3 to On to lock that step, then release. Play, then stop: only step 2 changes, to 65. The strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.

scenes.title: Let the channel inherit the global setting

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1. Quantise Note Mask works on three levels, strongest first: a step lock, then the channel value, then the global option. On follows the scale, Off keeps the written pitch, and X means inherit from the next level down. The state is listed as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: On / Off / X / On. The channel Off beats the global On and step 2 has its own On lock, so the strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.

steps.title: Channel: X inherits the global On
steps.caption: State: On / X / X / On. With no step held, turn the channel value down to X (unset). The global On applies again: 62, 65, 71, 60. Step 2 keeps its own On lock.

steps.title: Step: switch one step Off
steps.caption: State: On / X / Off / On. Hold step 1, turn E3 one detent up from X to Off and release. Play, then stop: step 1 plays its written note, 60, even though the global option is On. The strip reads 60, 65, 71, 60.

steps.title: Global: turn full quantisation Off
steps.caption: State: Off / X / Off / On. Press K1, open the Mosaic params and turn Quantise note masks Off. The channel value is still X, so it follows the global Off. Play, then stop: steps 3 and 4 play as written and step 2 keeps its On lock, 60, 65, 69, 71.

scenes.title: Let the channel beat the global setting

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1. Quantise Note Mask works on three levels, strongest first: a step lock, then the channel value, then the global option. On follows the scale, Off keeps the written pitch, and X means inherit from the next level down. The state is listed as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: Off / X / Off / On. The global Off is inherited by the channel, step 1 is Off and step 2 is On, so the strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.

steps.title: Channel: On beats the global Off
steps.caption: State: Off / On / Off / On. With no step held, turn E3 two detents up to On. Play, then stop: the channel On beats the global Off, so steps 3 and 4 follow the scale again, 60, 65, 71, 60.

steps.title: Step: clear an Off, then try an explicit X
steps.caption: First hold step 1, press K2 and release: the Off lock clears and the channel On applies. Play, then stop: 62, 65, 71, 60 (state Off / On / X / On). Then hold step 1, turn E3 all the way down to X and release. An explicit step X skips the channel and uses the global option directly, here Off, so step 1 plays its written note: 60, 65, 71, 60.

scenes.title: Clear a note mask without clearing its neighbour

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. The Masks page (Channel tasks, then Masks) is open on Note. The channel's Note mask default is 67 (G3), step 1 has its own mask 72 and step 2 has 74, so the MIDI strip reads 72, 74, 67, 67.

steps.title: Clear step 1 only
steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4), press K2 and release. Step 1 falls back to the channel default, 67, but step 2 keeps its 74. Play, then stop: the strip reads 67, 74, 67, 67.

steps.title: A held step wins over the shift clear
steps.caption: Hold step 1 again, hold K1 and press K2, then release. With a step held, only that step is cleared, even while K1 is down, and step 1 has nothing left to clear. Play, then stop: the strip still reads 67, 74, 67, 67.

steps.title: Clear every step mask on the channel
steps.caption: With no step held, hold K1 and press K2. Every step exception clears but the channel default stays. Play, then stop: the strip reads 67, 67, 67, 67.

scenes.title: Return a chord shape to X

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. On the Masks page Chd1 is set on every step to E, F, G and A (64, 65, 67, 69), and no strum is set. Trig params is open with no slot assigned. When played, each step sends its root first and then its chord note, both at the same moment: the MIDI strip lists C3 then E3, D3 then F3, and so on. Only the order of the two messages differs, so the effect is easy to miss without a Strum.

steps.title: Assign Chord Pattern and leave it at X
steps.caption: Press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Pattern in the parameter list, then press K3 to assign it and K2 to return. The slot reads X, which means no shape. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop: every root still sounds first, as before.

steps.title: Reverse the whole channel
steps.caption: With no step held, turn E3 two detents up to <- (reverse). Tap Play, then stop: on all four steps the chord note's Note On now comes before the root's, so the strip lists E3 then C3, F3 then D3, and so on. Nothing is strummed, so both still sound together; add a Strum to hear the order.

steps.title: Give two steps an explicit X
steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 all the way down to X and release; do the same on step 3. A step's own X beats the channel's setting. Tap Play, then stop: steps 1 and 3 send the root first again, while steps 2 and 4 keep the reverse order.

steps.title: Return the channel to X
steps.caption: With no step held, turn E3 two detents down to X. Steps 1 and 3 already read X; now every step does. Tap Play, then stop: all four roots come first again.
